## Solution

**Setup.** A smooth hyperquadric $Q \subset \mathbb{P}^5_{\mathbb{C}}$ is a degree-2 hypersurface defined by a nondegenerate quadratic form $q$ on $\mathbb{C}^6$. Over $\mathbb{C}$ all nondegenerate quadratic forms on $\mathbb{C}^6$ are equivalent, so we may take $q = x_0^2 + x_1^2 + x_2^2 + x_3^2 + x_4^2 + x_5^2$ with associated bilinear form $B(u,v) = u^\top v$.

A projective 2-plane $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{P}^5$ corresponds to a 3-dimensional vector subspace $W \subset \mathbb{C}^6$, and $\Lambda \subset Q$ iff $q|_W \equiv 0$ (i.e., $W$ is **totally isotropic**).

**Parameter space and expected dimension.** The Grassmannian $G(2,5)$ of projective 2-planes in $\mathbb{P}^5$ has dimension
$$\dim G(2,5) = (5-2)(2+1) = 9.$$
The restriction $q|_\Lambda$ is a quadric on $\mathbb{P}^2$, i.e., an element of $H^0(\mathbb{P}^2, \mathcal{O}(2))$, which has dimension $\binom{2+2}{2} = 6$. The condition $\Lambda \subset Q$ is the vanishing of these 6 sections, giving expected dimension
$$9 - 6 = 3.$$

**The condition is exact (tangent space computation).** We verify the Fano variety is smooth of dimension 3 at an explicit point. Take the totally isotropic subspace
$$W = \operatorname{span}\{v_1,\, v_2,\, v_3\}, \quad v_1 = e_0 + ie_1,\; v_2 = e_2 + ie_3,\; v_3 = e_4 + ie_5.$$
Indeed $q(v_j) = 1 + i^2 = 0$ and $B(v_j, v_k) = 0$ for all $j,k$, so $W$ is totally isotropic. Its complementary isotropic subspace is $W' = \operatorname{span}\{e_0 - ie_1,\, e_2 - ie_3,\, e_4 - ie_5\}$, with $\mathbb{C}^6 = W \oplus W'$ and $B(v_j, v'_k) = 2\delta_{jk}$.

The tangent space to $F_2(Q)$ at $W$ is
$$T_W F_2(Q) = \big\{\varphi \in \operatorname{Hom}(W,\, \mathbb{C}^6/W) : B(w_1, \varphi(w_2)) + B(w_2, \varphi(w_1)) = 0 \;\;\forall\, w_1, w_2 \in W\big\}.$$
Identifying $\mathbb{C}^6/W \cong W'$ and writing $\varphi(v_j) = \sum_k \varphi_{jk}\, v'_k$, we compute
$$B(v_j, \varphi(v_l)) = \sum_k \varphi_{lk}\, B(v_j, v'_k) = 2\varphi_{lj}.$$
The tangent condition becomes $\varphi_{lj} + \varphi_{jl} = 0$, i.e., $\varphi$ is **skew-symmetric**. The space of $3 \times 3$ skew-symmetric matrices has dimension $\binom{3}{2} = 3$.

Therefore $\dim T_W F_2(Q) = 3$, confirming the Fano variety is smooth of the expected dimension at this point (and by homogeneity of the quadric, everywhere).

**Conclusion.** Since $F_2(Q)$ is nonempty (given) and smooth of dimension 3 at every point,

$$\boxed{\dim F_2(Q) = 3}$$
